sections.normalized_html: The graph of the function [MATH: f] is a line in the [MATH: xy]-plane. If the line has slope [MATH: \dfrac{5}{6}] and [MATH: f(0) = -4.] Find the equation representing this line.
sections.readable_text: The graph of the function [MATH: f] is a line in the [MATH: xy]-plane. If the line has slope [MATH: \dfrac{5}{6}] and [MATH: f(0) = -4.] Find the equation representing this line.

sections.normalized_html:
We want to determine the equation of the function in the form [MATH: y = mx + b,]

where [MATH: m] is the slope and [MATH: b] is the [MATH: y]-intercept.

We are told the line has a slope [MATH: m = \frac{5}{6}.]

Since we know [MATH: f(0) = -4,] this means the line crosses the [MATH: y]-axis at [MATH: -4,] so the [MATH: y]-intercept is [MATH: b = -4.]

So, the equation of this line is [MATH: y = \frac{5}{6}x - 4.]

Therefore, since [MATH: y = f(x),] the equation that defines [MATH: f] is [MATH: f(x) = \frac{5}{6}x - 4.]

    • The line has the [MATH: y]-intercept [MATH: b \approx 3,] which satisfies [MATH: -1 \leq b \leq 3.] [MATH: \color{darkgreen}\checkmark]

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only".

[MATH: b = -4.]

So, the equation of this line is
[MATH: y = \frac{5}{6}x - 4.]

Therefore, since [MATH: y = f(x),] the equation that defines [MATH: f] is
[MATH: f(x) = \frac{5}{6}x - 4.]
